p.src: Now, because of this heavy snowfall, Wu Yong devised a stratagem in Song Jiang's camp, and by means of it they captured Suo Chao amid the snow. The rest of the troops fled back into the city and reported that Suo Chao had been captured. When Grand Secretary Liang heard the news, he could not help but panic. He ordered all his commanders merely to hold fast and forbade them to give battle. He wished to kill Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu, yet feared that this would enrage Song Jiang. Since the court had no troops ready to come to his aid, it would only hasten disaster. He therefore had no choice but to keep the two men under guard, send another report to the capital, and await Grand Tutor Cai's decision. Meanwhile, Song Jiang returned to camp and seated himself in the central command tent. The ambush troops soon brought Suo Chao before him. Song Jiang was overjoyed to see him. He ordered the soldiers away, personally untied Suo Chao, invited him into the tent, and offered him wine, soothing him with kindly words: “Look at my brothers here—more than half of them were officers of the imperial court. But because the court is benighted, allowing corrupt officials to dominate and venal officers to wield power and cruelly oppress innocent people, they have all willingly joined Song Jiang to carry out Heaven's justice. If you do not disdain us, General, let loyalty and righteousness be our common cause.” Yang Zhi stepped forward and exchanged a separate formal greeting with him, then urged him at length to join them. Suo Chao was destined to be numbered among the Heavenly Spirits; the time had naturally come for them to unite, and so he submitted to Song Jiang. That night they laid a feast in the tent to celebrate.

p.src: The next day they discussed how to attack the city. They assaulted it for several days in succession but could not break through. Song Jiang was deeply troubled. That night, as he lay with his head upon the pillow in his tent, a chill wind suddenly sighed about him and a piercing cold closed in. Song Jiang raised his head and saw the Heavenly King Chao Gai hovering as though he wished to approach but dared not, calling, “Brother, if you do not turn back now, what are you waiting for?” There he stood before him. Song Jiang started in alarm, rose hastily, and asked, “Elder brother, where have you come from? Your wrongful death remains unavenged, and my heart has known no peace by day or night. And of late I have offered no sacrifices to you. Since you have now appeared in spirit, surely you have come to rebuke me.” Chao Gai said, “That is not why I have come. Step back, brother. The force of the living breath about you is too strong, and I dare not draw near. I have come especially to warn you: within a hundred days you will suffer a bloody calamity, and only the Earthly Efficacious Star south of the Yangzi can cure you. Withdraw your army without delay; that is your best course.” Song Jiang wished to learn more and hurried forward, saying, “Elder brother, since your spirit has come here, I beg you to tell me the whole truth.” Chao Gai gave him a shove, and he awoke with a start—it had all been a dream beneath the southern bough. He immediately ordered a junior officer to summon the military adviser to interpret the dream. Wu Yong came to the central command tent, and Song Jiang told him of the strange occurrence. Wu Yong said, “Since the Heavenly King Chao has manifested his sacred presence, we cannot disregard his warning. The weather is bitterly cold and the ground frozen; our troops and horses cannot remain here long. Let us return to the mountain for the time being. When winter has ended and spring begins, and the snow and ice have melted, it will not be too late to return and attack the city.” Song Jiang said, “Your counsel is most sound, Adviser. But Squire Lu and our brother Shi Xiu are fettered in prison, where each day seems a year, and they look only to us brothers to come to their rescue. If we should simply return home, I truly fear those villains will take their lives. Whether we advance or retreat, the choice is difficult.”

p.src: Their deliberations remained unresolved. The next day Song Jiang felt his spirits exhausted and his whole body aching. His head seemed split by an axe and his body steamed as if in a basket; he took to his bed and could not rise. All the chieftains came to see him. Song Jiang said, “My back feels terribly hot and painful.” When they looked, they saw a red swelling raised like a griddle. Wu Yong said, “This illness must be either a boil or a malignant carbuncle. I have read in medical formularies that mung-bean powder can protect the heart and prevent the poison from invading it. We should buy some at once and prepare it for our elder brother to take.” At the same time they sent men in search of medicines and treatment, but nothing could cure him. Then Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, said, “When I lived by the Xunyang River, my mother once suffered from a disease of the back. No medicine could cure her, but later we obtained the services of An Daoquan of Jiankang Prefecture, and the moment he treated her, the illness vanished. Thereafter, whenever I came by a little silver, I would have someone take it to him. Now that I see our elder brother stricken with this illness, I know the road eastward is long and that he cannot be brought here quickly. But for our elder brother's sake, I must travel night and day and respectfully invite him here.” Wu Yong said, “In our elder brother's dream, the Heavenly King Chao said, ‘For the calamity within a hundred days, only the Earthly Efficacious Star south of the Yangzi can provide a cure.’ Can this be the very man the prophecy foretold?” Song Jiang said, “Brother, if you know such a man, go to him quickly on my behalf. Do not shrink from the hardship, but put brotherhood first. Travel night and day, invite this man here, and save my life.” Wu Yong had a hundred taels of garlic-clove gold brought out for the physician, as well as twenty or thirty taels of loose silver for traveling expenses. He instructed Zhang Shun, “Set out this very moment. Whatever happens, you must bring him back with you; on no account may there be any delay. I shall now break camp and return to the mountain, so meet us with him at the stronghold. Brother, make all possible haste.” Zhang Shun took leave of them all, slung his bundle over his back, and set off.

p.src: Meanwhile, the military adviser Wu Yong issued an order to all the commanders: “For the present, withdraw the army, cease hostilities, and return to the mountain.” They placed Song Jiang in a cart and set out that very night. The men inside Beijing had already suffered from an ambush stratagem and assumed this was another lure, so they dared not pursue. The next day, when Grand Secretary Liang received the report, he said, “We do not know what they mean by this withdrawal.” Li Cheng and Wen Da said, “That scoundrel Wu Yong has innumerable cunning schemes. We should merely hold fast and must not give chase.” The tale now divides into two. To return to Zhang Shun: intent on saving Song Jiang, he hurried onward night and day. It was the end of winter; when it did not rain, it snowed, and the journey was extremely arduous. Moreover, in his haste he had brought no rain gear. After traveling for more than ten days, he was already nearing the Yangzi River. That day a fierce north wind arose, and frozen clouds hung low. Snow whirled and scattered until it covered the whole sky. Braving wind and snow, Zhang Shun pressed on at the risk of his life, determined to cross the great river. p.src: A lone goose cries through frozen clouds; cold crows circle above the withered trees. Snow falls from the sky like pear blossoms, flakes of scattered jade whirling everywhere. Jade weighs down the wine banner by the bridge; silver carpets the fishing boats at the ferry. Two or three homes show faintly in the village ahead; at evening the river makes a scene fit for a painting.

p.src: Zhang Shun ran alone to the bank of the Yangzi. When he looked for a ferryboat, there was not one in sight, and he could only lament his ill fortune. He walked along the riverbank and saw smoke rising from among some withered reeds and broken rushes. Zhang Shun called out, “Boatman! Bring your ferry quickly and take me across!” There came a rustling from the reeds, and a man emerged, wearing a bamboo-leaf hat and a straw rain cape. He asked, “Where do you wish to go, traveler?” Zhang Shun said, “I must cross the river and go to Jiankang Prefecture on urgent business. I will pay you extra, so please take me over.” The boatman said, “I do not mind taking you, but it is late today. Even if you cross now, you will have nowhere to lodge. Rest in my boat for now. At the fourth watch, when the wind has died and the moon is bright, I will take you across—but you must pay me a little more.” Zhang Shun said, “That is reasonable.” He followed the boatman into the reeds. A small boat was moored by the shoal, and beneath its awning a thin young man sat warming himself at a fire. The boatman helped Zhang Shun aboard and led him into the cabin. Zhang Shun took off all his wet clothes, and the boatman told the young man to dry them over the fire. Zhang Shun opened his bundle, took out a quilted blanket, wrapped it around himself, and lay down in the cabin. He asked the boatman, “Is there anywhere here that sells wine? It would be good to buy some to drink.” The boatman replied, “There is nowhere to buy wine, but you may have a bowl of rice if you want.” Zhang Shun ate a bowl of rice, laid down his head, and went to sleep. He was worn out from many days of hardship and, moreover, had been far too careless; by about the first watch he had unwittingly fallen fast asleep. The thin young man sat by the charcoal fire, drying the patched jacket he wore over his clothes. Seeing that Zhang Shun was asleep, he called to the boatman, “Elder brother, do you see?” The boatman crept over and gave the bundle by Zhang Shun’s head a squeeze. Feeling that it held gold and valuables, he motioned with his hand and said, “Cast off the boat. We can do the deed once we reach midstream.” The young man pushed aside the awning, leapt ashore, untied the mooring rope, and came back aboard. He pushed off with a bamboo pole, set the oar in place, and rowed creaking and groaning out toward midstream. Inside the cabin the boatman took the mooring rope and gently bound Zhang Shun hand and foot into a bundle. Then he went to the stern and drew a broad knife from beneath the planking. At that moment Zhang Shun awoke, but with both hands bound he could not struggle free. The boatman, great knife in hand, pinned him down. Zhang Shun said, “Good fellow, spare my life, and I will give you all my gold.” The boatman replied, “I want the gold, and I want your life as well.” Zhang Shun cried repeatedly, “At least let me die whole, and my wronged ghost will not return to haunt you.” The boatman put down his broad knife and, with a splash, threw Zhang Shun into the water.

p.src: When the boatman opened the bundle and saw the great quantity of gold and silver inside, he no longer wished to share it with the thin young man. He called, “Fifth Brother, come here—I have something to tell you.” The young man ducked into the cabin. The boatman seized him with one hand and brought down his knife, hacking him to pieces, then shoved him into the water. The boatman cleaned away the bloodstains in the boat and rowed off alone.

p.src: Now Zhang Shun was a man who could remain underwater for three or five nights. The moment he was thrown in, he sank to the riverbed, bit through the rope, and swam underwater to the southern bank, where he saw a faint light among the trees. Zhang Shun clambered ashore, dripping wet, and made his way into the woods. There he found a village wineshop where they had risen in the middle of the night to press wine; lamplight shone through cracks in its broken wall. Zhang Shun called until the door was opened. On seeing an old man, he bowed his head to the ground before him. The old man said, “Were you robbed on the river and forced to leap into the water to save your life?” Zhang Shun replied, “To tell you the truth, venerable sir, I came to Jiankang on business. It grew late, and while I was looking for a boat across the river, I unexpectedly fell in with two villains. They robbed me of all my clothes, gold, and silver, then flung me into the river. But I know how to swim underwater and managed to escape with my life. Please help me, grandfather.” Hearing this, the old man led Zhang Shun into a back room, gave him a patched jacket to wear while his wet clothes were dried, and warmed some wine for him to drink. The old man asked, “What is your surname, good fellow? What business brings a man from Shandong here?” Zhang Shun replied, “My surname is Zhang. Imperial Physician An of Jiankang Prefecture is a brother of mine, and I have come especially to visit him.” The old man said, “Since you came from Shandong, did you pass by Liangshan Marsh?” Zhang Shun said, “I came by that very place.” The old man said, “Chief Song on that mountain neither robs passing travelers nor takes human life. He acts only to uphold Heaven’s justice.” Zhang Shun said, “Chief Song holds loyalty and righteousness above all. He does not harm honest folk, but condemns corrupt officials and venal functionaries alone.” The old man said, “I have heard that Song Jiang and his band are truly humane and righteous, forever helping the poor and aiding the aged. How can they be compared with the petty bandits here? If only they would come here, the common people could live happily and no longer suffer the harassment of this gang of corrupt officials!” When Zhang Shun had heard him out, he said, “Do not be alarmed, grandfather. I am Zhang Shun, the ‘White Streak in the Waves.’ My elder brother Song Gongming is suffering from a malignant carbuncle on his back, so he sent me with a hundred taels of gold to summon An Daoquan. Who would have thought that I would be so careless as to fall asleep in the boat? Those two wretches bound my hands and threw me into the river. I bit through the rope, however, and made my way here.” The old man said, “Since you are one of the heroes from that stronghold, I shall call my son out to meet you.” Before long a young man came out from the rear. At the sight of Zhang Shun, he bowed and said, “I have long heard of your great name, elder brother, but until now fate has denied me the honor of meeting you. My surname is Wang, and I am the sixth among my brothers. Because I am quick in running and leaping, everyone calls me Wang Dingliu, the ‘Living Goddess of Lightning.’ All my life I have loved swimming underwater and wielding the staff. I have often sought out teachers, but never received true instruction, so for now I make my living selling wine by the river. I know both of the men who robbed you just now. One is Zhang Wang, the ‘River-Blocking Demon.’ The other, the thin young man, is a native of Huating County named Sun the Fifth, known as the ‘Loach in Oil.’ Those two scoundrels often rob people on this river. Set your mind at ease, elder brother, and stay here a few days. When that rogue comes to drink, I will avenge you.” Zhang Shun said, “I am deeply grateful for your kindness, brother. But for the sake of my elder brother Song Gongming, I long to hurry back to the stronghold without losing even a day. I shall wait only until dawn, then enter the city, bring back Imperial Physician An, and return to meet you.” Wang Dingliu gave Zhang Shun his own clothes to change into. He hastened to prepare wine and entertain him; there is no need to relate the details. The next day the sky cleared and the snow melted. They gave Zhang Shun more than ten taels of silver and sent him on into Jiankang Prefecture.

p.src: Once inside the city, Zhang Shun went straight to Locust Bridge, where he saw An Daoquan selling medicine before his door. Zhang Shun entered the house, and on seeing An Daoquan, bowed his head to the ground before him. There is a poem devoted solely to praising An Daoquan’s excellence:

p.src: An Daoquan had inherited both internal medicine and surgery from his ancestors and could treat every kind of ailment; thus his fame had spread far and wide. When he saw Zhang Shun, he asked, “Brother, I have not seen you for many years. What wind has blown you here?” Zhang Shun followed him inside and related in full how he had caused an uproar at Jiangzhou and followed Song Jiang to the mountain stronghold. Then he explained that Song Jiang was suffering from a carbuncle on his back and that he had come expressly to fetch the divine physician; and that he had nearly lost his life on the Yangzi River and therefore arrived empty-handed, telling him the whole truth. An Daoquan said, “As for Song Gongming, he is a righteous man renowned throughout the realm. It would be best for me to make the journey. But my poor wife has passed away, and I have no other relatives at home. I cannot go far away, which makes it difficult for me to leave.” Zhang Shun pleaded earnestly, “If you refuse to go, elder brother, I too will find it impossible to return to the mountain.” An Daoquan said, “Let us discuss it further.” Only after Zhang Shun had implored him in every possible way did An Daoquan finally consent. p.src: That evening An Daoquan took Zhang Shun with him to her house, where wine was laid out for them. Li Qiaonu paid her respects to Zhang Shun as an uncle. After several cups, when they were half drunk, An Daoquan said to Qiaonu, “I shall spend tonight here with you. Early tomorrow I will travel with this brother to Shandong. At most I shall be gone a month, or as little as twenty-odd days, and then I will return to see you.” Li Qiaonu said, “I will not have you go. If you do not heed me, never come through my door again!” An Daoquan said, “I have already packed my medicine bag and need only set out. I shall leave tomorrow. Set your mind at ease. Even though I go, I shall not be delayed.” Li Qiaonu pouted and played the coquette, collapsing into An Daoquan’s arms and saying, “If you still refuse to heed me and go away, I shall curse you until your flesh flies off in pieces!” Hearing this, Zhang Shun wished he could swallow the woman in a single gulp of water. As the hour grew late, An Daoquan fell down dead drunk. He was helped into Qiaonu’s room and laid upon the bed. Qiaonu then came to dismiss Zhang Shun, saying, “Go home now. There is nowhere for you to sleep in my house.” Zhang Shun replied, “I shall wait until elder brother wakes, and then we will leave together.” Since she could not make him budge, she had no choice but to lodge him in a small room by the front door.

p.src: Zhang Shun was tormented by anxiety and could not sleep. During the first watch, someone knocked at the door. Peering through a crack in the wall, Zhang Shun saw a man slip inside and begin speaking with the old procuress. The old woman asked, “Where have you been that you have not come for so long? Tonight the physician is lying drunk in her room. What are we to do?” The man said, “I have ten taels of gold for elder sister to buy hairpins and bracelets. Mother, find some way to let her meet with me.” The procuress said, “Wait in my room. I will call my daughter here.” When Zhang Shun looked through the lamplight, he saw that it was Zhang Wang, the River-Cutting Ghost. It turned out that whenever this rogue obtained any wealth on the river, he came to spend it at her house. At the sight of him, Zhang Shun could no longer restrain his fury. Listening more closely, he heard the procuress prepare food and wine in the room and summon Qiaonu to keep Zhang Wang company. Zhang Shun was about to burst in, but then feared he might spoil matters and let the villain escape. Around the third watch, the two kitchen servants were drunk as well, while the procuress swayed to and fro, blinking drowsily before the lamp. Zhang Shun quietly opened his door and slipped into the kitchen, where he saw a gleaming kitchen knife lying upon the stove; he saw the procuress sprawled upon a bench at the side. Zhang Shun entered, picked up the kitchen knife, and first killed the procuress. When he turned to kill the servants, he discovered the knife was none too sharp: after hacking one person, its edge had already curled over. Just as the two were about to cry out, he spied a wood-splitting axe close at hand, snatched it up, and struck them down, one with each blow. Hearing the noise, the woman in the room hurriedly opened the door and ran straight into Zhang Shun. His arm rose, the axe fell, and he struck her across the chest, felling her to the floor. In the lamplight Zhang Wang saw the woman struck down. He pushed open the rear window, leapt over the wall, and escaped. Zhang Shun was bitterly frustrated. At once he cut off a piece of his robe, dipped it in blood, and wrote upon the plastered wall: “The killer is An Daoquan!” He wrote it dozens of times.

p.src: He waited until the fifth watch, when dawn was about to break, and then heard An Daoquan wake from his drunken sleep and call for Qiaonu. Zhang Shun said, “Elder brother, do not make a sound. I have two people to show you.” An Daoquan rose and saw four corpses. Terror numbed his whole body, and he trembled in a heap. Zhang Shun said, “Elder brother, do you see what is written on the wall?” An Daoquan cried, “You have ruined me!” Zhang Shun said, “There are only two paths open to you. If you raise an alarm, I shall leave by myself, while you, elder brother, will have to pay with your life; but if you wish to remain unharmed, fetch your medicine bag from home and make straight for Liangshan Marsh tonight to save my elder brother. The choice between these two is yours.” An Daoquan said, “Brother, what a fatally reckless thing you have done!” A poem bears witness:

p.src: At daybreak, Zhang Shun gathered up the travel money and returned home with An Daoquan. They knocked open the door, took the medicine bag, left the city, and went straight to Wang Dingliu's tavern. Wang Dingliu received them and said, “Zhang Wang passed by here yesterday. What a pity he did not meet you, elder brother.” Zhang Shun said, “I have important business to attend to. I shall put aside this petty vengeance for now.” Before he had finished speaking, Wang Dingliu announced, “That scoundrel Zhang Wang is coming.” Zhang Shun said, “Do not alarm him yet. Let us see where he goes.” They saw Zhang Wang go to the riverbank to inspect his boat. Wang Dingliu called, “Brother Zhang, keep your boat here and take two relatives of mine across.” Zhang Wang replied, “If they want the boat, have them come quickly!” Wang Dingliu reported this to Zhang Shun. Zhang Shun said, “Brother An, lend me your clothes to wear. Put on mine, and then we shall go aboard.” An Daoquan said, “What is the meaning of this?” Zhang Shun replied, “I have a plan. Do not ask, brother.” An Daoquan took off his clothes and exchanged them with Zhang Shun. Zhang Shun put on the headcloth and pulled the brim of the dust-shielding warm hat low to conceal himself. Wang Dingliu shouldered the medicine bag and walked to the boat. Zhang Wang brought the boat alongside the bank, and the three men boarded. Zhang Shun crawled into the stern and lifted a deck board to look beneath it. The broad-bladed sword was still there. Zhang Shun took it and went back into the cabin. Zhang Wang rowed away, the oars creaking as the boat went straight into midstream. Zhang Shun cast off his outer covering and cried, “Boatman, come quickly! Look, water is leaking into the cabin!” Unaware that it was a trick, Zhang Wang thrust his head into the cabin. Zhang Shun seized him firmly and shouted, “You vicious thief! Do you recognize the passenger who took your boat on that snowy day?” When Zhang Wang saw him, he could not utter a sound. Zhang Shun shouted, “You scoundrel, you plotted to rob me of a hundred taels of gold and even tried to take my life! Where has that skinny young fellow gone?” Zhang Wang said, “Hero, after I got the treasure, I had no wish to share it with him. Fearing he would quarrel over it, I killed him and threw him into the river.” Zhang Shun said, “Do you know who I am?” Zhang Wang replied, “I do not know you, hero. I beg you only to spare my life.” Zhang Shun roared, “I was born beside the Xunyang River and raised beneath Mount Xiaogu. I worked as a fish broker—who did not know me? After causing an uproar in Jiangzhou, I joined Liangshan Marsh and followed Song Gongming across the realm—who does not fear me? You scoundrel opened a leak in my boat, bound my hands, and threw me into midstream. Had I not known how to swim, I would have lost my life! Today enemies meet face to face. I cannot spare you!” With that, he dragged Zhang Wang into the cabin, bound his hands and feet together like four horse hooves, trussed him into a bundle, and, taking aim at the mighty Yangzi River, hurled him straight in. “That saves you from the stroke of my blade!” As for Zhang Wang's life, it was plain that by dusk he would be a ghost. Wang Dingliu watched and sighed deeply. Zhang Shun searched the boat and found the gold from the other day, together with some loose silver. He packed it all away, and the three rowed the boat ashore. Zhang Shun said to Wang Dingliu, “Worthy brother, I shall never forget your kindness and loyalty as long as I live. If you do not disdain the proposal, you and your father may close up the tavern and hasten to Liangshan Marsh, where we can join together in the righteous cause. What do you think?” Wang Dingliu replied, “What you say, elder brother, is exactly what I desire.” After saying their farewells, Zhang Shun and An Daoquan set out from the northern bank. Wang Dingliu took leave of the two, boarded the small boat again, and returned home to prepare his baggage and follow them.

p.src: Now Zhang Shun and An Daoquan reached the northern bank, shouldered the medicine bag, and immediately set off. An Daoquan, however, was a man of letters and unused to walking. Before they had covered more than thirty li, he could go no farther. Zhang Shun invited him into a village tavern and bought wine for him. While they were drinking, a traveler came up from outside and cried, “Brother, why have you been delayed so long?” When Zhang Shun looked, he saw that it was Dai Zong, the “Magic Traveler,” disguised as a traveler and hurrying after them. Zhang Shun hastily introduced him to An Daoquan, then asked for news of Brother Song Gongming. Dai Zong said, “Brother Song is now delirious. He takes neither water nor rice and is plainly near death.” Hearing this, Zhang Shun's tears fell like rain. An Daoquan asked, “What is the color of his skin and flesh?” Dai Zong replied, “His flesh is wasted. He cries out all night, and the pain never ceases. His life may fail at any moment.” An Daoquan said, “If his flesh and body can still feel pain, he can be cured. I fear only that we may arrive too late.” Dai Zong said, “That is easily managed.” He took two magic traveling talismans and fastened them to An Daoquan's legs. Dai Zong shouldered the medicine bag himself and instructed Zhang Shun, “Come at your own pace. I shall go ahead with the physician.” The two left the village tavern, invoked the magic traveling art, and went on ahead.

p.src: Meanwhile, Zhang Shun rested for two or three days at the village tavern. Then Wang Dingliu duly arrived with his father, carrying a bundle on his back. Zhang Shun received them with great delight and said, “I have stayed here expressly to wait for you.” Wang Dingliu asked, “Where is Physician An?” Zhang Shun replied, “Dai Zong, the ‘Magic Traveler,’ came to meet us, and has already gone ahead with him.” Wang Dingliu then set out with Zhang Shun and his father, bound for Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Meanwhile, Dai Zong led An Daoquan onward with the magic traveling art and reached Liangshan Marsh after traveling all night. All the chiefs of the stronghold came to receive them and escorted them into Song Jiang's bedchamber. When they looked at him on the bed, his breath came only in the faintest gasps. An Daoquan first felt his pulse, then said, “Chiefs, do not be alarmed. There is nothing wrong with his pulse. Though his condition appears grave, it is not serious in the main. I do not say this in boast, but within ten days he will be restored to his former health.” On hearing this, everyone bowed together. An Daoquan first used heated moxa to draw out the poison, and then administered medicine. Externally he applied medicinal plasters, and internally he gave strengthening draughts. Within five days, the color gradually returned to his skin, his flesh grew supple, and he began to take more food. Before ten days had passed, though the wound had not completely closed, his appetite had returned to normal. Then Zhang Shun arrived with Wang Dingliu and his father. They paid their respects to Song Jiang and the other chiefs, and recounted the robbery on the river and the vengeance taken upon the water. Everyone exclaimed in admiration, “Brother's illness very nearly went untreated!” As soon as Song Jiang had recovered, he consulted with Wu Yong about attacking Beijing to rescue Squire Lu and Shi Xiu. An Daoquan remonstrated, “General, your wound has not yet closed. You must not move about lightly; if you do, it will be very difficult to heal.” Wu Yong said, “Do not trouble yourself over this, brother. Attend only to your recovery and restore the vital primal energy within your body. Though I possess little ability, within the present season I am determined to break through the walls of Beijing, save the lives of Squire Lu and Shi Xiu, and seize the adulterous woman and her paramour. What do you think, brother?” Song Jiang said, “If the strategist will support me so, I could die without regret!” Wu Yong immediately issued orders in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. The result would be that within Beijing's walls, there arose a fiery pit and a forest of spears; and throughout Daming Prefecture, mountains of corpses and seas of blood. Indeed: At his easy words, ghosts and spirits all lose courage; at his command, every hero yields his heart. What plan the strategist Wu Yong ultimately proposed will be revealed in the next chapter.

Wu Yong immediately issued orders in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness.
The result would be that within Beijing's walls, there arose a fiery pit and a forest of spears;
and throughout Daming Prefecture, mountains of corpses and seas of blood.
Indeed: At his easy words, ghosts and spirits all lose courage; at his command, every hero yields his heart.
What plan the strategist Wu Yong ultimately proposed will be revealed in the next chapter.
